# Protocol: the three Twitter files the memory gate excluded (frozen 2026-10-23, before any download of the new files)

**Why now.** `docs/twitter_sampled_extension_protocol.md` and `docs/twitter_sample10_extension_protocol.md` excluded clusters 29 and 41 (sample10, about 25 M distinct objects each) and 32 (sample100, 35.6 M objects) because the peak-memory estimate then in force (1 GiB + 250 bytes per object) put them above what the machine could allow. The estimate was later lowered to 1 GiB + 100 bytes per object after every completed run peaked at 0.3-2.3 GB, which puts the three at 3.5, 3.5 and 4.6 GiB, inside the gate. They are therefore tried, under the same rules.

**Inputs.** `twitter/sample10/cluster29...sample10.zst` (4.35 GB), `twitter/sample10/cluster41...sample10.zst` (2.04 GB) from the CMU PDL mirror, and the already downloaded `twitter/sample100/cluster32...sample100.zst`. Identity checks (HEAD length, `zstd -t`, SHA-256, exact distinct-object count), 12 policies x 2 cache sizes with exact capacities, controlled seed 42, one result root per file, live guards (12 GiB process RSS, 4 GiB MemAvailable) unchanged: a run that crosses a guard stays omitted and is listed, with one retry pass when memory frees up. Nothing else changes from the sample10 batch.

**Reporting.** Results join the Figure 3c/3f union as labelled sampled clusters; no hypothesis is attached. Variant Amendment 7's held-out-3 set is **not** extended (it was fixed on 2026-10-21 and its rule is closed).

## Outcome (2026-10-23; 66 of 72 runs, `local_results/twitter_gated_extension/gated_extension.csv`)

All 66 runs the gate allowed completed with exact counters. The six omitted are CACHEUS on the three files at both sizes (estimate above the 12 GiB soft budget; no run was attempted). **Consequence for the reporting rule:** the Figure 3c/3f union requires all of the paper's algorithms on a cluster, and CACHEUS is missing, so **these three clusters do not join the union** (the rule in "Reporting" said they would; it could not be met, and the union stays at 44 / 45 clusters). Their results are reported on their own:

| cluster (file) | cache | SIEVE reduction from FIFO | SIEVE rank among the 11 algorithms run | best algorithm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 29 (sample10) | 0.1% | 0.154 | 4 | TwoQ 0.287 |
| 29 (sample10) | 10% | 0.152 | 3 | TwoQ 0.171 |
| 41 (sample10) | 0.1% | -0.066 | 10 | LHD 0.212 |
| 41 (sample10) | 10% | 0.038 | 4 | LRU 0.050 |
| 32 (sample100) | both | 0.000 | tie | none: 97.0% of the 36.7 M requests are first accesses (35,575,740 distinct objects), every policy misses 0.970004 |

The 11 algorithms run are FIFO, LRU, CLOCK, SIEVE, ARC, TwoQ, LIRS, LHD, Hyperbolic, TinyLFU and B-LRU (B-LRU's miss ratio is 1.0 on cluster 32 because its admission filter admits nothing on a stream with no reuse). On these two sample10 files SIEVE is not the top algorithm at either size, which is the paper's pattern for a minority of Twitter clusters and agrees with the shape of Figure 5's Twitter panel (SIEVE wins a share of the traces, not all); with two clusters this is a count, not a test. Cluster 32 as a 1% sample has almost no reuse, so it cannot discriminate between policies; whether the full trace does, we did not measure. Identity files are `cluster*_identity.json` in the same folder.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-25, before any CACHEUS run on these files): the six omitted CACHEUS cells

The CACHEUS cells were omitted by an estimate of 0.5 GiB + 600 B per object (above the 12 GiB budget). `docs/metakv_split_protocol.md` (outcome of amendment 2) measured ten CACHEUS runs on 16-17 M objects: peak RSS 0.77 GiB at the 0.1% cache and at most 2.45 GiB at 10% (151 B per object at most), so those estimates were about four times too high. Files and runs are otherwise as in this protocol: clusters 29 and 41 (about 25 M objects) and 32 (35.6 M), CACHEUS only, seed 42, exact capacities, one worker at a time, estimate 0.5 GiB + 160 B x objects (`TWITTER_EXT_CACHEUS_PER_OBJECT=160`: the measured maximum plus 6%, extrapolated to 25-36 M objects, which is a larger scale than measured). The live guard (12 GiB process-tree RSS, 4 GiB available RAM) stays; a run it stops is an omission with its reason. **Consequence for the reporting rule.** If all six cells complete, the three clusters have all 12 policies of Figure 3 and join the Figure 3c/3f union as labelled sampled clusters, as the original "Reporting" paragraph said; if any cell is omitted they stay outside it, as now.

**Amendment 2a (2026-10-25, after clusters 29 and 41 finished, before cluster 32 ran).** Clusters 29 and 41 completed (four cells, peak RSS 0.80-1.06 GiB at the 0.1% cache and 1.33-1.69 GiB at 10%, at most 73 B per object on 25 M objects). Cluster 32 (35.6 M objects) was omitted by the pre-run gate at 160 B per object (needs 9.80 GiB available, the machine had 8.57 GiB); nothing had run on it. For the remaining two cells the estimate is 0.5 GiB + 100 B x objects (`TWITTER_EXT_CACHEUS_PER_OBJECT=100`): the measured maximum on the same trace family (73 B) plus 37%. This is lower than the 151 B per object measured on the Meta KV traces, so the live guard (12 GiB RSS, 4 GiB available RAM) is what protects the machine; a stopped run is an omission with its reason.

## Outcome of amendments 2 and 2a (2026-10-25): 72 of 72 runs; the three clusters join the Figure 3c/3f union

All six CACHEUS cells completed (cluster 29: 0.1% 147,219,726 misses of 698,889,960 requests, peak RSS 1.05 GiB; 10% 34,832,782, 1.65 GiB; cluster 41: 76,616,994 of 320,359,608, 0.79 GiB; 27,410,084, 1.33 GiB; cluster 32: 35,575,740 of 36,675,855 at both sizes, 0.86 and 1.56 GiB), none stopped by the guard. The original 600 B per object CACHEUS estimate was 8 times too high on these files (at most 73 B per object). The reporting rule of the first paragraph therefore applies: with all 12 policies, clusters 29, 41 and 32 join the union, which becomes **47 clusters at the 10% cache and 48 at 0.1%** (it was 44 and 45); the rank correlation of the 11 algorithms' means with the paper's is 0.991 / 0.982 (0.989 / 0.982 before), SIEVE's mean 0.160 / 0.093 (0.167 / 0.097 before; paper 0.153 / 0.083). Cluster 32 contributes zero reductions for every algorithm (97% of its requests are first accesses), and cluster 41 a negative SIEVE reduction at 0.1% (-0.066), so the three clusters pull SIEVE's mean down by 0.007 and 0.004. The Variant study's held-out set (Amendment 7) is not extended; its rule closed on 2026-10-21.
